questions.question: What download speed does Kestrel guarantee on Fibre 900, and what happens if my speed falls below it?
questions.reference_answer: The minimum guaranteed download speed on Fibre 900 is 450 Mbps (kd_04). If the average of three wired tests on three different days is below that, the customer reports it, and Kestrel has 30 calendar days from the report to restore the speed. If it doesn't, the customer can leave without an early termination charge or move to a slower plan without a new minimum term (kd_04).
assertions: The response gives the minimum guaranteed download speed as 450 Mbps.
The response says that Kestrel has 30 calendar days from the report to restore the speed.
The response says that the customer can leave without an early termination charge if the speed isn't restored.

questions.question: What does a solid red light on my KR-3 router mean?
questions.reference_answer: A solid red light means that the router is getting no signal from the Kestrel network. The customer should check both ends of the network cable and restart the router, and report a fault on 01632 960150 or online if the light stays red (kd_08).

The response tells the customer to check the cable and restart the router before reporting a fault.

questions.question: Will Kestrel slow my connection in the evening if I download a lot?
questions.reference_answer: No. The current fair use policy says that Kestrel doesn't cap data and doesn't slow or manage traffic at any time of day because of how much a customer uses, and that Kestrel stopped managing traffic in 2024 (kd_05). The traffic management policy that describes evening slowdowns above 250 GB a month was last reviewed in March 2022, covers plans that Kestrel no longer sells, and is out of date, so it must not be used to answer.
assertions: The response says that Kestrel doesn't slow connections because of how much the customer downloads.
The response doesn't present an evening slowdown or a 250 GB threshold as current policy.

questions.question: I'm moving house next month. How much notice do I need to give, and is there a charge to move my broadband?
questions.reference_answer: The customer should tell Kestrel at least 14 days before moving. If the plan is available at the new address, it moves at no charge, and the monthly price and minimum term stay the same (kd_11).
assertions: The response says that the customer must give at least 14 days' notice.
The response says that there is no charge to move the plan when it is available at the new address.

questions.question: I'm on Essential 80 with 6 months of my minimum term left. How much will it cost me to leave now?
questions.reference_answer: The early termination charge is the monthly price multiplied by the whole months left, less 20 per cent (kd_12). Essential 80 costs £26.00 a month (kd_02), so the charge is £26.00 × 6 = £156.00, less 20 per cent, which is £124.80. The customer must also give 30 days' notice and return the router within 30 days of the service ending, or pay £50.00 (kd_12).
assertions: The response gives the early termination charge as £124.80.
The response mentions the 30-day notice period.

questions.question: What happens if I don't pay my bill?
questions.reference_answer: If a direct debit fails, Kestrel tells the customer and tries again 5 days later. A £7.50 late payment fee is added if a bill is still unpaid 14 days after its due date, and broadband is suspended if it is still unpaid 28 days after its due date. The customer can ask billing to spread an overdue balance over up to 3 months (kd_25).
assertions: The response gives the late payment fee as £7.50 after 14 days.
The response says that broadband is suspended after 28 days unpaid.
The response mentions that a payment plan of up to 3 months is available.

questions.question: Will my home phone work in a power cut?
questions.reference_answer: Not on its own. The digital voice service runs through the router, so the home phone stops working in a power cut unless a battery backup unit is fitted. The unit is free for priority support customers and for customers with no mobile signal at home, and it costs £45.00 for other customers (kd_23).
assertions: The response says that the home phone doesn't work in a power cut without a battery backup unit.

questions.question: How do I make a complaint, and when can I take it to the independent scheme?
questions.reference_answer: The customer can complain by phone, by email or online. Kestrel acknowledges a complaint within 2 working days and sends a final response within 8 weeks. If the customer is unhappy with the final response, or if 8 weeks have passed without one, they can refer the complaint to the independent dispute resolution scheme free of charge (kd_17).
assertions: The response says that Kestrel sends a final response within 8 weeks.
The response says that the customer can go to the independent scheme after the final response or after 8 weeks.

questions.question: A customer in the KT-04 area reports no service, and the status board shows a declared outage for that area. Should I book an engineer visit?
questions.reference_answer: No. When an outage is declared for the customer's area, link the case to the incident reference and don't book an engineer visit. Give the customer only the estimated restoration time from the status board, and update the case at least every 4 hours while the incident is open (kd_13).
